clause: a second bring-up REUSES the binding it already made instead of minting a duplicate
now_false: NOT THE DANGER, WHICH IS CLOSED MORE STRONGLY THAN THE SENTENCE PROMISED — no bring-up mints a duplicate binding, because no bring-up mints a binding at all. What is false is the MECHANISM this sentence names, and a mechanism is what a reader re-runs. `69a89134 feat(up)!: a repository binding is remote configuration, not a dotenv copy` deleted ensureRepositoryBinding together with the dotenv reader beside it: resolveRepository now only GETs /v1/repository-bindings and REPORTS the rows the deployment already holds, because a binding names a real repository, a real branch and — with a connection_ref — a real credential, which is remote configuration the console's /repositories screen already owned. Two paths to one binding was the defect that week was spent deleting, and the dotenv path was the worse of the two in a specific way: it could not express a connection_ref at all, so a binding a bring-up created was STRUCTURALLY the one that could never publish. So there is no 'binding it already made' for a second bring-up to reuse, and the idempotence this clause asserted is not satisfied — it is VACUOUS. Two further halves of the same sentence went with it and are recorded here rather than left implicit: the retarget leg (changing PALAI_GIT_BASE_BRANCH minted a NEW binding, so a pull request could not keep targeting a branch the operator had stopped asking for) has no subject any more, and PALAI_GIT_CLONE_URL / PALAI_GIT_BASE_BRANCH / PALAI_GIT_REPO have no reader in this command at all. A reader re-running this clause looks for an idempotent create and finds a read.
evidence: `grep -rn 'ensureRepositoryBinding' --include='*.go' --include='*.sql' --include='*.sh' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.yaml' --include='*.yml' . | grep -v ./evidence/` -> 0 (2026-08-05). The proof CAS-001 listed for this clause is gone with it: `git show HEAD:cmd/cli/internal/stack/up_repository_test.go | grep -c 'func TestABringUpReusesTheRepositoryBindingItAlreadyMade'` -> 0. Its replacement is STRONGER than the clause rather than a rename of it, which is why it is not substituted in as a survivor: cmd/cli/internal/stack/up_repository_test.go:TestTheBringUpREPORTSBindingsAndCreatesNone SETS all three dotenv variables while the bring-up runs and FAILS on any POST to /v1/repository-bindings, so it refuses the return of the path instead of restating its absence — a version that only checked the report would have passed against the old code too. Zero writes on every bring-up is a wider guarantee than one reuse on the second, and it is a different sentence.

clause: a surface the stack does not mount is reported rather than swallowed
now_false: FALSE AND DELIBERATELY INVERTED, which is exactly why it is recorded here instead of being re-pointed at the guard that replaced it. A control plane wired no BindingRegistrar leaves the three /v1/repository-bindings routes unmounted and answers 404. resolveRepository now returns an empty repositoryBinding{} on any error or non-200 — no id and NO WARNING — and nothing downstream speaks either: both call sites print only repo.resolved and repo.warn (Bootstrap's own report and reportRepositoryBinding), and workspacelessBindingWarning returns the empty string the moment repo.id is empty. That is precisely 'swallowed'. THE TRADE IS THE RIGHT ONE and this record does not argue with it: 'could not ask' is not 'there are none', and a command that only REPORTS bindings must not warn on a 404, because that warning sends an operator to create something they may already have. But it is a TRADE, and this clause is the side of it that was given up. WHAT MUST NOT BE READ INTO THE REPLACEMENT: TestAnUnreadableBindingSurfaceDoesNotClaimThereAreNone proves this sentence's NEGATION — it FAILS if a warning is produced for an unreadable surface — so it is evidence that the clause is false and can never be a re-pointing of it under a new name. WHAT SURVIVES IS THE NEIGHBOURING CLAUSE, which is a different fact about a different condition and keeps a proof of its own: 'a missing configuration WARNS instead of skipping silently' still holds, for a deployment holding ZERO bindings rather than for one whose surface cannot be read, and the warning now names the /repositories screen that fixes it.
evidence: The same deleted symbol carries both rows, and the reason is the reason for this one: warning on a 404 was correct only while this function CREATED bindings — a create that cannot reach its surface has FAILED, while a read that cannot reach its surface has only failed to ANSWER — which is what `69a89134`'s own message states ('the old code warned on a 404, which was right when it CREATED bindings and wrong now that it only reports them'). Measured 2026-08-05 on HEAD 9ad0665d: `git show HEAD:cmd/cli/internal/stack/up_repository_test.go | grep -c 'func TestARepositorySurfaceTheStackDoesNotMountIsReportedRatherThanSwallowed'` -> 0, and the function that replaced it asserts `repo.warn == ""` against an httptest server answering 404 to everything. `git show HEAD:cmd/cli/internal/stack/up.go | grep -c 'repo.warn'` -> 3, and all three are gated on a non-empty string — one through appendWarn, which returns the slice unchanged for "" — so an empty warn reaches no operator by any path. The commands are carried rather than the line numbers because `9ad0665d` moved this function 130 lines the same day. The clause was true when published and has been false since 2026-08-05 16:03:20 +0300.
